privacy.metaDescription: How Menuyukti collects, uses, and protects data in your workspace.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy

data.title: Data we process
data.body: Menuyukti processes information you provide when you use the product—including account details, location and sales data you upload, workflow and milestone content, and usage needed to run the service. We process this data to deliver analytics, workflows, and AI-assisted features you request.

use.title: How we use your data
use.body: We use your data to operate and improve the platform, provide support, secure accounts, and comply with law. We do not sell your personal information or your restaurant sales data to third parties for their marketing.

sharing.title: Service providers
sharing.body: We may use trusted subprocessors (for example hosting, authentication, and AI inference) that process data under contract and only as needed to provide the service. A current list can be provided on request.

security.title: Security
security.body: We apply reasonable technical and organizational measures designed to protect your information. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure; we encourage strong passwords and safe sharing of workspace access.

cookies.title: Cookies and analytics
cookies.body: Menuyukti loads Google Analytics 4 only on our print shop pages (/shop), and only after you accept analytics in the cookie banner. If you choose Essentials only, no analytics scripts are loaded and no analytics cookies are set. You can change your choice anytime via the Cookie settings link in the footer.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: For privacy-related questions or requests, contact us through the same channel you use for Menuyukti product support.

terms.metaDescription: Terms governing use of the Menuyukti platform.
terms.title: Terms of Service

service.title: The service
service.body: Menuyukti provides software for restaurant marketing workflows, analytics, and related AI-assisted features. Features may change as the product evolves.

account.title: Your account
account.body: You are responsible for activity under your account and for keeping credentials secure. You agree to provide accurate information and to use the service in compliance with applicable law.

acceptable.title: Acceptable use
acceptable.body: You may not misuse the service, attempt to access others’ data without permission, interfere with operation of the platform, or use the service to violate law or third-party rights.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.body: The service and any AI-generated outputs are provided on an “as is” basis. Analytics and suggestions are informational; you remain responsible for business and compliance decisions.

changes.title: Changes
changes.body: We may update these terms or the service. Continued use after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated terms where permitted by law.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.q1: What data do I need to upload?
faq.a1: For Pro workflows and sales-grounded AI analytics, upload your POS sales report (where your POS format is supported) so we can normalize columns and build demand, mix, and timing signals. Studio AI generation and strategy chat do not require sales data to be useful; the print shop never requires uploads.
faq.q2: Do I need sales data to use Studio or the print shop?
faq.a2: No. Studio and strategy chat do not require sales uploads. Connecting reports unlocks smarter, evidence-backed Pro automation. The print shop is standalone artwork you can browse anytime as an add-on.
faq.q3: What is an agentic AI system?
faq.a3: An agentic AI system goes beyond a single chat reply: it can plan steps, call tools, and run multi-milestone workflows toward a goal—like a teammate following a brief. In Menuyukti, that shows up strongest in Pro campaign pipelines that turn sales signals into schedules, promotion ideas, and copy. You stay in control with inspectable runs and workspace data, while the system handles repetitive orchestration.
faq.a4: Restaurant owners, operators, and solo marketers who run social media for small to mid-sized restaurants and want faster Instagram execution with stronger data-backed decisions.
faq.a5: Yes. You can share workflows, milestones, and brand assets when you bring in collaborators.

That pixel count supports crisp vertical posters up to roughly 18×24 inches at 300 DPI; you can crop or rotate for other layouts if needed. promotion_candidates.label: Promotion candidates
promotion_candidates.title: Promotion candidates
promotion_candidates.inputDescription: Optional guidance for ideas and emphasis (themes, categories to stress, tone, or constraints). Sent with menu-engineering analytics when you run this milestone.
promotion_candidates.inputPlaceholder: e.g. Push brunch cocktails and vegetarian mains; avoid deep-fried items in copy…
promotion_candidates.goal: The data documents promotion-ready menus from menu engineering: when POS categories exist, one block per `menu_category` with star and puzzle highlights; when categories are missing, a flat summary instead. Include 3–8 grounded `promotionIdeas` tied to real menu names from analytics.
promotion_candidates.criterionGrouping: **Grouping** in the data matches the tool (`by_menu_category` or `flat`).
promotion_candidates.criterionCategoriesOrFlat: When grouped, **categories** keys match POS `menu_category` strings; each block lists `starHighlights` and `puzzleHighlights` from the tool. When flat, **flatSummary** explains the candidate set and **categories** stays empty.
promotion_candidates.criterionPromotionIdeas: **Promotion ideas** include 3–8 unique non-empty items, each referencing a real menu from `topStars` or `topPuzzles` in the tool output.

post_scheduler.label: Post scheduler
post_scheduler.title: Post scheduler
post_scheduler.inputDescription: Optional guidance for cadence, Reels vs feed posts, dayparts, or weekend/holiday preferences. The run still uses prior Dates, Brand Brief, and Promotion Candidates from this workflow.
post_scheduler.inputPlaceholder: e.g. 3 posts per week; avoid weekends; prefer Reels for hero dishes…
post_scheduler.goal: Generate a list of Instagram posts for the campaign window: each entry has weekday, date, time, post type (Reel or Post), content type (Carousel or Single), promoted menu items from prior promotion data, and a caption idea aligned with the brand brief.
post_scheduler.criterionPostsGenerated: **Posts** in the data is a non-empty array when the campaign dates and promotion context support a schedule; otherwise document why the list is empty.
post_scheduler.criterionPostFields: Each post includes **dayOfWeek**, **date** (YYYY-MM-DD), **time**, **postType** (`Reel` or `Post`), **contentType** (`Carousel` or `Single`), **promotedMenuItems**, and **captionIdea**. For multi-post schedules, include a format mix: at least one `Reel` and one `Post`, plus at least one `Carousel` and one `Single`.
post_scheduler.criterionMenuItems: **Promoted menu items** only name dishes that appear in the prior Promotion Candidates milestone (ideas or highlights), not invented items.

restaurant_brand_brief.label: Brand brief
restaurant_brand_brief.title: Brand brief
restaurant_brand_brief.inputDescription: Optional context for generation (style, positioning, constraints). Example: during a soccer World Cup period, note campaign priorities or tone for match days. Included with location and analytics data when you run or generate the brief.
restaurant_brand_brief.inputPlaceholder: e.g. Family-friendly trattoria tone; highlight lunch and vegetarian options…
restaurant_brand_brief.goal: The data holds a factual location-only brand brief: venue snapshot, 3-5 content pillars tied to operating/category signals, 3-5 audience hypotheses supported by available analytics, 3-5 proof-oriented angles grounded in menu/category signals, and 3-5 tone guardrails. The data must not include campaign start or end dates for this milestone.
restaurant_brand_brief.criterionVenueSnapshot: **Venue snapshot** in the data names the venue and uses city/country/currency when known; it does not invent full addresses and does not add campaign start/end dates.
restaurant_brand_brief.criterionContentPillars: **Content pillars** include 3-5 unique non-empty items tied to real categories or operating signals (for example meal periods or weekday vs weekend patterns).
restaurant_brand_brief.criterionAudienceHypotheses: **Audience hypotheses** include 3-5 unique non-empty items reflecting only what the data supports (for example peaks, meal periods, weekday/weekend split); no invented demographics.
restaurant_brand_brief.criterionProofAngles: **Proof-oriented angles** include 3-5 unique non-empty items and reference real menu/category signals already present in the data (for example top items or category mix).
restaurant_brand_brief.criterionToneGuardrails: **Tone guardrails** include 3-5 unique non-empty items and stay consistent with operating context in the data.

chat.milestone2ResultMarkdown:
## Workflow brief

**Goal:** lift weekday lunch covers by 8% over 4 weeks.

**Audience:** office workers within 10 minutes, Tue–Thu 11:30–1:30.

**Messages:** speed of service, chef’s lunch set, loyalty nudge.

**Channels:** Instagram feed + Stories; in-store QR to follow.

chat.milestoneHelpBrandBriefOptionalInputHowU: If you fill the optional Input field, it is sent alongside location profile and analytics signals when generating the brand brief.
chat.milestoneHelpBrandBriefOptionalInputWhen: Use it when temporary context or constraints matter, for example during a soccer World Cup period (match-day audience, campaign tone, offers, or no-alcohol messaging). Leave it empty when standard analytics and profile data are enough.
chat.milestoneHelpPromotionCandidatesOptional: If you fill the optional Input field, it is sent with promotion-engineering analytics when generating candidates and ideas. The model uses it for emphasis and tone; it must still only reference real menu names from the analytics output.
Use it when you want a seasonal theme, channel focus, or categories to highlight. Leave it empty when the default menu-engineering picks are enough.
chat.milestoneHelpPostSchedulerOptionalInputH: If you fill the optional Input field, it guides posting cadence, format mix (Reels vs feed), timing, and whether to skip weekends or holidays via the available-dates tool. Prior workflow milestones still supply dates, holidays, brand tone, and promotion items.
chat.milestoneHelpPostSchedulerOptionalInputW: Use it when you have scheduling constraints (e.g. weekdays only, more Reels, lunch-focused times). Leave it empty when the default spread across the campaign window is fine.
chat.milestoneHelpOptionalInputSummary: Notes from the Input tab are free-form guidance for the run; they are not verified as analytics facts.
